title: Vector integration is invariant under an isomorphism over a fixed base
statement: Let N>0, let A be a finite commutative ring killed by N, and let S be Noetherian with N invertible. Let F and G be locally free modules of the same rank d on S, with compactifiable vector-bundle projections p:E(F)->S and q:E(G)->S and q quasi-compact. Given any scheme isomorphism e:E(G) ~= E(F) with e.hom;p=q, form the Cartesian square with top e.hom and bottom id_S. Write Q=A_S(d)[2d], W=p*Q and Wprime=q*Q. Let beta:(id_S)*Rp_!W -> Rq_!e*W be actual compact-support exchange and let c:e*p*Q ~= q*Q be the inverse of the pullback compositor for e;p=q. Then the identity-pullback inverse comparison, followed by beta, Rq_!(c), and the actual integration of G, equals the actual integration of F. No base morphism between different bases, purity family, zero-section preservation or linearity hypothesis is present. The arbitrary total-space isomorphism may be nonlinear. Rank zero, the empty base and the zero ring are included.

source.place: paragraph 2, scalar integration and degree-zero descent; parent lem-pur-vector-integration-cartesian-trace proof step 2, invariance under the presentation isomorphism

proof.text: Cover S by the pairwise intersections of finite-rank frame opens for F and G. Restrict the two module frames to each intersection W. Each inverse frame is a Cartesian affine chart over W into S. Compose the G chart with e and use uniqueness of the two pullbacks of E(F) over W to construct a genuine automorphism a of the single affine coordinate tower. Its hom composed with the F chart equals the G chart followed by e, and a lies over id_W. No linearity of a is asserted.

Prove directly that the given fixed-base exchange, after inverse-image restriction to W and the G chart prefix, is the Cartesian prefix for the G chart followed by e. The coefficient equation is the associativity equation for inverse-image compositors; the exchange equation is horizontal pasting, naturality in the coefficient, and the right identity law. Identify the chart coefficients with the generic Cartesian coefficients by the equality-transport formula for the compositor. Apply the existing Cartesian-prefix action equation to a.

Choose the normalized line data provided by the affine-space top trace. The normalization of vector integration identifies the two frame restrictions with the respective prefixes followed by this ordered counit. The affine-space isomorphism trace-invariance lemma removes the a-action. This gives equality of the two maps after restriction to W, with the constant-object comparison cancelled.

Use the canonical gluing identification of the F compact-support source with a sheaf placed in degree zero. Fullness of the single functor writes each global derived map as a sheaf map after this identification. Naturality of the degree-zero restriction correspondence turns the preceding local equalities into equalities of inverse-image sheaf maps. The jointly surjective frame cover is jointly conservative and hence jointly faithful in the abelian category, so the two global sheaf maps agree. Their single-functor images give the desired derived equality. This argument uses neither nonemptiness, nonzero coefficients, nor positive rank.

theorem vectorIntegration_presentationIso
    (N : ℕ) (hN : 0 < N) (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [Finite A]
    (hA : (N : A) = 0) (S : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian S]
    (hS : IsUnit (N : Γ(S, ⊤))) (d : ℕ) (F G : S.Modules)
    [F.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank d] [G.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank d]
    [HasCompactification (VectorBundleZeroSection.π S d F)]
    [HasCompactification (VectorBundleZeroSection.π S d G)]
    [QuasiCompact (VectorBundleZeroSection.π S d G)]
    (e : VectorBundleZeroSection.scheme S d G ≅ VectorBundleZeroSection.scheme S d F)
    (he : e.hom ≫ VectorBundleZeroSection.π S d F = VectorBundleZeroSection.π S d G)
    (sq : IsPullback e.hom (VectorBundleZeroSection.π S d G)
      (VectorBundleZeroSection.π S d F) (𝟙 S)) :
    (leftDerivedUpperStarId (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) S).inv.app
        (vectorIntegrationSource A N hA S d F) ≫
      (rightDerivedLowerShriekBaseChangeMap A sq).app
        (vectorIntegrationCoefficient A N hA S d F) ≫
      (rightDerivedLowerShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)
        (VectorBundleZeroSection.π S d G)).map
        ((leftDerivedUpperStarComp (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) e.hom
          (VectorBundleZeroSection.π S d F) (VectorBundleZeroSection.π S d G)
          he.symm).inv.app (affineLinearBaseCoefficient A N hA S d)) ≫
      vectorBundleIntegration N hN A hA S hS d G =
    vectorBundleIntegration N hN A hA S hS d F
